titel: Ask HTM - Overrated HSA, 13% Dividend Yields, & Getting Into Real Estate #1183

einzeiler: Listener Q&A on HSA viability, single stock investing, and real estate strategies.
kurzfassung: The hosts answer listener questions covering Health Savings Accounts, investing in single stocks and REITs, and getting started in physical real estate. They also discuss retirement cash bucket strategies and evaluate the pros and cons of live-and-flip real estate investing. Throughout the episode, they offer practical financial guidance paired with personal anecdotes.
stichpunkte: Most HSA holders fail to invest their balances, missing out on major tax-free compounding growth.
Combining an HSA with a Roth IRA provides a powerful multi-account retirement strategy.
Holding underperforming single stocks or REITs requires an honest assessment of portfolio allocation and sunk cost fallacy.
Buying and living in a property while renovating allows homeowners to capitalize on the $500,000 capital gains tax exclusion.
Self-managing rental properties locally often yields better results than hiring distant property managers.
Retirement cash buckets help mitigate the sequence of returns risk during market downturns.

kapitel.titel: Anniversary travel plans and Frontier Airlines woes
Are HSAs overrated? A deep dive into triple tax advantages
Dealing with underwater single stock investments and REIT dividends
Getting started in real estate investing and the live-and-flip strategy
Building retirement cash reserves and the bucket approach

clips.text: The hosts outline upcoming listener questions addressing individual stock purchases and two distinct approaches to property investing.
A listener weighs the long-term investment growth of health savings accounts against the reality of future currency devaluation.

clips.text: After discussing health account withdrawal rules, the speakers pivot to a 15-mile run and a newly opened French bakery in Chattanooga.

clips.hook: Exclude up to $500,000 in capital gains tax
clips.text: The conversation shifts to nationwide demographic shifts, noting steep population drops in northern hubs like Baltimore, Philadelphia, and Detroit.
